text: From the PEO-090 review: PEO-082 is the wrong lever (it batches updates, it does not cut per-update work, and it is an L design item). Brief plan: first dispatch the siege workflow on x86 to replace the 920 s projection with a real number; then either split siege.yml into 3 jobs, one per building, each running --check on its share (~5 min each), or record a 20 min on-demand budget in testing.md and the PEO-088 brief. Drop the PEO-082 reference. Do not cut hours, buildings or seeds (that changes N022, the user's call).
briefed: split siege.yml into one --check job per building (per-building baseline). x86 real number 704 s (run 37494258700), replaces the 920 s projection.

commits: 85f6d43 (per-building files + baseline split, no value moved: only headers differ, every row and map line unchanged and in order), c9a5e33 (siege.yml matrix A/B/C, fail-fast off, 20 min timeout, wall time on failure), 0531f01 (testing.md). tests: verify --frontend --full green; refusals --setup enclosed --check, --seeds 1 --write, --density heavy --building A --check all exit 2. CI: run 37846104838 on main, three jobs pass --check, peo_siege wall A 227 s, B 230 s, C 281 s (budget 600); siege-report-B artifact holds only building B. M1 (8 threads): old full --check 420 s before the split; --building A/B/C alone 358/414/467 s and full 848 s, each matching the baseline and each building's files byte-equal to the full run's, but these times are inflated by another process loading the machine (load avg 8-11) and are not a clean comparison. perf: on 8 threads one building's 12 runs are bounded by its slowest heavy runs, so locally a building is not a third of the full run; on the 4-vCPU CI runner it is (227-281 s vs 704 s). open: none.
